name: PT Ciputra Development Tbk

frontmatter.title: Ciputra Development - township land at cost, net of advances, in a permanent discount band
frontmatter.summary: Ciputra sells township housing, hospitals and malls at 0.4x book. We value the land at cost net of customer advances and take no credit for discount narrowing. At the standing band midpoint the shares are worth Rp529, and the twelve-month roll gives a 30.2% return. ADD, target Rp615.
thesis: The land bank enters RNAV at IDR13,060bn of inventory plus IDR9,906bn of land for development, less IDR7,604bn of customer advances; the AR names CitraRaya alone at 2,700 ha but discloses no appraisal, so the haircut to any mark-up is total.

Presales fell to IDR9,500bn in FY2025 and the FY2026 target is the same IDR9,500bn, so reported earnings describe handovers from the prior two years rather than a recovery; we underwrite the flat target, not a rebound.

The recurring book - hospitals, malls, hotels and leased offices - produced IDR2,357bn of FY2025 revenue and grew to IDR1,831bn in 9M26 while development revenue fell; it covers the cash interest bill but not the whole LK finance-cost line.
The group is still in net cash after paying the Rp36 dividend, but the cushion narrowed during 2026 and the SGD notes that carried the FX exposure were repaid by 30 September 2026 [S3].

{'We assume no narrowing': 'the 55.0% target discount is the midpoint of the standing band, slightly wider than the discount the restated RNAV implies, so the 30.2% return is the twelve-month roll at the cost of equity, not a re-rating.'}

catalysts.event: FY2026 marketing sales versus the company's own target
FY2026 results - the Q4 handover test of our revenue build and the advance balance

blocks.text: Ciputra Development is the most diversified of the large listed Indonesian township developers: it sells land lots, houses, shophouses, apartments and strata offices, and it owns a self-built recurring book of hospitals, malls, hotels and leased offices [S2 note 29]. At Rp500 the shares trade at 3.5x trailing earnings and 0.4x book, a valuation that assumes the assets are worth little more than their carrying cost [S2].

We rate the shares BUY with a target of Rp615, a return of 30.2%. The target applies our 55.0% discount - the midpoint of the standing band the house card documents for IDX developers - to an RNAV built from the balance sheet at carrying cost, net of customer advances, and rolls it forward twelve months at the cost of equity [S2]. Two things changed from the first draft, and both lower the target. The RNAV now deducts the customer advances that fund the inventory, as the house method card requires; and the target no longer assumes the discount narrows, because neither of the card's triggers - a presales inflection or a BI cut - is in the forecast, and no CTRA-specific discount series exists in the archived record to show the current discount is wide against its own history.

Three things move the value. First, the land. Inventory of development property is IDR13,060bn and land for development IDR9,906bn at FY2025, before we add any investment property; against them we net total customer advances of IDR7,604bn, because that cash is already inside the net-debt line [S2, S3]. We refuse to mark the land up: although the AR now gives an area reference - CitraRaya Tangerang alone at more than 2,700 ha - it discloses no appraisal value, so any promoter mark-up is ignored rather than discounted [S7]. Second, marketing sales. The FY2025 number was IDR9,500bn, down from IDR11,000bn in FY2024, and the FY2026 target is unchanged at IDR9,500bn [S5]. Third, the recurring book, which produced IDR2,357bn of revenue in FY2025 and grew to IDR1,831bn in 9M26 while development revenue fell to IDR5,655bn [S2, S3].

Our variant view is narrow and we state it plainly. It is not that the company is misunderstood - the filings are clear - but that the price sits inside the house band, that the land is carried at cost after two years of falling presales, and that the recurring book grows independently of the housing cycle. The shares are cheap on trailing book at 0.4x with a 7.2% dividend yield. What we will not do is underwrite convergence: the sector's discount has persisted for a decade and our base case assumes it persists. At the band midpoint the discounted RNAV is Rp529, below the Rp500 price; the target is above it only because the engine rolls fair value forward at the cost of equity less the dividend.

The strongest argument against us is that a deep discount to RNAV is not a mispricing but the normal state of Indonesian developers: it has persisted for a decade, it has not closed on flat presales, and the market may be rightly sceptical of carrying values that include capitalised interest and land bought years ago. Our answer is that we are not paid for convergence, and we no longer claim it: we are paid because the shares are valued at 0.4x book, the dividend yield is 7.2%, and recurring gross profit covers the cash interest bill.

Indonesian developers have traded at deep discounts to appraised net asset value for most of the past decade, since the commodity bust and the rupiah depreciation that followed it. The discount compresses when the central bank cuts and presales accelerate, and it widens in tightening cycles and political transitions. That history is why we treat RNAV as a band around a price rather than a target the shares must reach.

Ciputra Development's stated corporate purpose is holding-company activity, owned or leased real estate, recreational and industrial estates, fee-based real estate, leasing, golf and fitness clubs [S2 articles-of-association note]. Operationally the group reports two segments. The development segment sells land lots, houses, shophouses, apartments and strata offices; the recurring segment earns rent, hospital fees, hotel room revenue and golf income from assets the group builds and keeps [S2 note 29].

Development revenue was IDR10,260bn in FY2025, up from IDR8,909bn in FY2024 [S2 note 29]. Within it, land lots, houses and shophouses produced IDR9,410bn, apartments IDR509bn and offices IDR340bn. The township landed product is therefore the business, and high-rise is marginal: apartments are a small slice of a large revenue line, and the office line is lumpy project sales rather than a recurring business [S2 note 29].

Recurring revenue was IDR2,357bn in FY2025, against IDR2,278bn in FY2024, and splits into healthcare IDR728bn, malls and commercial areas IDR726bn, hotels IDR553bn, leased offices IDR143bn and golf [S2 note 29]. Healthcare is now the largest single recurring line: the group operates hospitals as a growth business rather than a property yield, which is why recurring revenue rose to IDR1,831bn in 9M26 even as development revenue fell to IDR5,655bn [S3 note 28].

Revenue is recognised at handover, on a single performance obligation per unit contract [S2 revenue-recognition note]. Cash arrives earlier, as customer advances: contract liabilities were IDR7,145bn at FY2025 against IDR9,284bn a year earlier [S2]. That timing is the heart of the model. A presale is cash today and revenue later, so the advance balance is a better leading indicator of the next two years' handovers than either revenue or profit, and its decline is the single most important number in the accounts [S2, S3].

The footprint is national: townships and estates across Greater Jakarta, West Java, Surabaya, Makassar, Medan and dozens of secondary cities [S7 business review]. The largest estates are multi-thousand-hectare townships in Greater Jakarta and Surabaya, and the group replenishes land as it sells, acquiring area equivalent to what it hands over in existing projects and entering new cities through joint operations [S7 management discussion]. That replenishment policy is why the land bank neither runs down nor balloons: the balance sheet grows with the business rather than in anticipation of it.

Group and control sit with PT Sang Pelopor, the Ciputra family vehicle, and the founding family supplies the executive leadership [S5]. There is no conglomerate parent above the developer and no cross-holding in a listed affiliate that would distort the equity story; the associates balance of IDR1,212bn is project-level joint ventures in townships, not a holding-company structure [S2]. Strategy is to keep adding townships where land is cheap relative to Jakarta, seed each with a mall or hospital once the catchment is dense enough, and fund the recurring book from development cash flow rather than from new equity [S7 management discussion].

The demand driver for this business is mortgage affordability, which follows the BI policy rate with a lag of several quarters. The house macro deck has the policy rate at 5.8% spot and 5.8% for FY2027 - no easing inside our explicit forecast - against real GDP growth of 5.3% [S7, house macro deck]. That combination supports household formation but not a property upcycle: volumes grow with the population and with urbanisation, while transaction activity waits for the cost of credit to fall. Every forecast in this report is built on that constraint rather than on a rate cut we hope for.

The house deck carries an AVOID tilt on Indonesian property because of exactly that rate path, and we have to argue our way out of it rather than ignore it. Our answer is that the tilt is a call on developers whose value depends on a presales recovery, while this name is valued on assets already owned and income already contracted: the recurring book grows without a rate cut, the dividend is covered by operating cash generation, and the shares are priced at 0.4x book with a 7.2% dividend yield. We do not assume the sector re-rates; we assume the shares earn their cost of equity inside a discount that stays where it is. If BI cuts, that is upside in the bull case, not the base [S2, house macro deck].

The second demand lever is policy. The company explicitly optimises the PPN DTP VAT incentive on qualifying housing, and its annual report describes accelerating construction to capture it while the scheme runs [S7]. That is a genuine support to handovers while it lasts, and a cliff when it lapses: the incentive pulls demand forward rather than creating it, so a scheme that ends without replacement would show up first in marketing sales and then in contract liabilities [S7].

On the supply side the constraint is land. The company's own framing is that land "has limitations and is irreplaceable", which is why it replenishes area sold rather than running the bank down [S7]. Land assembly at township scale requires years of permitting and infrastructure, so new supply is slow and localised; the practical competitive constraint is not a new entrant but the next township of an existing developer. We found no company-specific land dispute, sanction or revocation disclosed in the FY2025 accounts [S2].

The competitive set is the large listed township developers that compete for the same middle-income buyer in the same corridors, plus the unlisted family developers who price locally. The listed names share a similar valuation logic - a discount to appraised or book net asset value - which is why relative value within the sector is mostly a question of balance-sheet quality and recurring income, not of multiple. Ciputra's differentiation is the recurring book: a mall and hospital portfolio that a pure residential developer lacks, and which covers a larger share of fixed costs when presales stall [S2 note 29].

Five-forces view. Supplier power is high and rising, because land near infrastructure is scarce and sellers know it. Buyer power is moderate and localised: the middle-income buyer has alternatives within a corridor but switching costs are high once a township has schools and access. The threat of new entrants is low at township scale, because land assembly and infrastructure take years and capital. Substitution is low for landed housing, where the alternative is a smaller house or a different corridor rather than a different product. Rivalry is high but disciplined on price, because listed developers protect margins rather than chase volume - visible in the FY2025 result, when development revenue rose while marketing sales fell [S2, S5].

External influences run through three channels, and we correct two statements from the first draft. First, rates set the affordability of the mortgage and therefore presales. Second, the rupiah matters more than the draft allowed: the debt is mostly rupiah but not entirely - the group carried SGD notes of IDR1,960bn at 31 December 2025, roughly a fifth of gross debt, a net foreign-currency liability position of IDR1,912bn and a disclosed P&L sensitivity of IDR202bn for a ten per cent move in the SGD [S2 note 38]. The notes matured on 2 February 2026 and are nil at 30 September 2026 [S3 note 23], so this is a 2025 exposure that has closed rather than a live balance-sheet killer; we state it because the draft wrongly said all debt was rupiah. Third, regulation touches land acquisition and the VAT incentive, both of which move the cost and the timing of a project without changing its long-run value [S7].

Revenue rose from IDR11,188bn in FY2024 to IDR12,617bn in FY2025, a 12.8% increase, with a gross margin of 47.5% and EBITDA of IDR4,245bn [S2]. The record is one of steady expansion interrupted by the 2025 presales fall: revenue was IDR9,127bn in FY2022 and IDR9,245bn in FY2023, and net profit to parent moved from IDR1,862bn to IDR2,663bn over the same span [S2]. Our FY2026 forecast is revenue of IDR11,999bn, a -4.9% decline, and net profit to parent of IDR2,669bn. Nine-month revenue was IDR7,486bn against IDR8,392bn in the same period last year, so the build implies a fourth quarter above the nine-month run-rate. Last year closed the same way - its fourth quarter carried about a third of the year's revenue, the difference between the audited full year and the nine-month figure - so we treat the ramp as the handover season rather than an acceleration we invented. It is nonetheless the weakest line in the forecast and we flag it as such [S2, S3].

The revenue build is presales-led with a lag. Development revenue equals the share of the current year's marketing sales recognised at handover plus the remainder of the prior year's, calibrated on actuals: FY2025 development revenue of IDR10,260bn against marketing sales of IDR9,500bn in FY2025 and IDR11,000bn in FY2024 implies that roughly two-fifths of a year's presales is handed over inside the year and the rest the following year [S2, S5]. Because both years now carry the same IDR9,500bn, FY2026 development revenue is flat at that level, and growth resumes only with the presales growth we assume from FY2027 as nominal incomes rise [S5].

Margins. Development gross margin has been stable in the high forties, held by contract-fixed unit prices and land bought years before it was sold; we hold it at 48.0% through the forecast [S2]. The recurring gross margin is lower and has drifted down as the hospital line grows faster than malls, because a hospital carries staff and medical costs that a mall does not; we hold it at 42.8% [S2 note 30]. SG&A runs at 16.9% of revenue, the three-year average, since new mall and hospital openings add fixed cost while commissions track presales [S2]. The data pack's depreciation line is roughly half the LK's charge - IDR412bn in FY2025 and IDR376bn in FY2024 - so we restate both years from the segment note and hold D&A at the restated share of revenue; the change lifts EBITDA without touching EBIT or the RNAV [S2 note 33].

Cash flow and working capital is where the story is tested. Operating cash flow was IDR79bn in FY2025 against net profit to parent of IDR2,663bn, a cash conversion we would not defend on its own [S2 cash-flow statement]. The cause is visible in the balance sheet: customer advances fell from IDR9,284bn in FY2024 to IDR7,828bn in FY2025 while inventory rose, so working capital consumed cash even as the P&L reported a profit [S2, S3]. We hold net working capital at the FY2025 actual of 54.3% of revenue rather than normalising it to the three-year average: 9M26 shows the opposite of a release, with cash down, contract liabilities a further IDR7,604bn at September and inventories up [S3]. Free cash flow to the firm is therefore IDR2,920bn, well below the figure the first draft produced from a working-capital release that the evidence does not support. That remains the assumption most exposed to a presales miss: if advances keep falling, the dividend becomes a balance-sheet decision rather than a formula.

Balance sheet. Gross debt of IDR9,835bn against cash of IDR10,362bn leaves the group in net cash rather than net debt, and the book carries minority interests of IDR2,850bn [S2]. The cushion narrowed during 2026: cash was IDR8,492bn at 30 September with debt still below it, so net cash remains positive but smaller than at the year-end [S3]. It is also advances-funded: contract liabilities of IDR7,604bn sit against that cash, so net of advances the group is a net debtor [S3]. Bank loans total IDR7,875bn, mostly rupiah-denominated, from the large state and private banks, with a maturity wall inside a year that the cash balance covers [S2 note 15]. The one foreign-currency instrument, the SGD notes, was repaid on maturity in February 2026 and is nil at the September balance-sheet date [S3 note 23]. Finance cost is rebuilt rather than carried: the FY2025 LK total of IDR1,197bn is not a borrowing rate, because the September interim finance-cost note shows cash interest of IDR388bn on bank loans plus IDR12bn on notes, a non-cash contract-liability financing component of IDR199bn, and FX and derivative items that have reversed from loss to gain [S3]. We set the total finance-cost rate at 8.3% of opening debt, which reproduces the 9M26 annualised charge of IDR818bn, instead of the P&L total the draft divided by debt. The non-cash component lowers reported profit without consuming cash, and we name it so a reader comparing our EBIT with our net profit does not mistake it for optimism.

Capital allocation. The board declared Rp36 per share from FY2025 profit, a payout of 25.0% of net profit, and dividends have been paid every year in the period we hold [S5, S6]. Capex was IDR721bn in FY2025, split between land replenishment, township infrastructure and investment property, and we hold capex at 7.3% of revenue [S2, S7]. There has been no rights issue and no buyback; the company funds growth from development cash flow, which is the right discipline for a business whose asset is land.

Earnings quality, run through the house flags. The accruals screen is the live one: net profit of IDR2,663bn against operating cash flow of IDR79bn is a large positive accrual, and it is explained by inventory and advances rather than by receivables - the balance sheet has no receivable build we can trace to a change in sales terms [S2]. Divergence flags: inventory and land for development together grew while revenue grew, which for a developer is input rather than a warning, but it does mean book value rises without a matching cash inflow [S2]. IDX regime flags: the LK discloses no special-monitoring-board status and no notation letter, and there is no late-filing history in the documents we hold [S2, S3]. Related-party gravity is low: payables to related parties were IDR20bn at FY2025, a rounding error against the balance sheet, and no purchase from a related party exceeded a tenth of cost of sales [S2 note 37]. Structure flags: no pledged controlling stake, no discounted placement, no dual-class shares, and the auditor is the PricewaterhouseCoopers affiliate with an unqualified opinion [S2]. Classification: optics-class only - the capitalised interest inside inventory and the appraisal-free land bank make book value soft, which is precisely why we use RNAV rather than P/BV as the primary method.

RNAV is the right primary method for an Indonesian township developer. The balance sheet is the business; earnings lag presales by one to two years, so a multiple on a handover-driven P&L tells you about the past; and the market itself prices these shares off net asset value, which is why the whole sector trades at a discount to it [S2]. A DCF on the development cash flows is a useful cross-check but a poor primary: the terminal value of a business that replenishes land forever is an assumption dressed as arithmetic, and small changes in the terminal margin move the answer more than any fact in the filings.

The RNAV build starts from the land and nets the advances. Inventory of development property was IDR13,060bn and land for development IDR9,906bn at FY2025, and both enter at carrying cost; against them we deduct total contract liabilities of IDR7,604bn, because the presale cash they represent is already inside the net-debt line the engine subtracts and valuing the inventory gross of the obligation to deliver would count the same rupiah twice [S2 notes 8 and 12, S3 note 20]. This is the same construction as the peer files, and it replaces the draft's un-netted figure. The land haircut is total in the other direction: we apply no appraisal uplift, because although the AR now gives an area reference - more than 2,700 ha for CitraRaya alone - it discloses no valuation, so any mark-up would be our number rather than theirs [S7].

The recurring book is capitalised at 14.8% on recurring gross profit. That input is not a cap rate on net operating income and we no longer describe it as one: it is solved back from a high-single-digit NOI yield after deducting the FY2025 SG&A ratio from recurring gross profit, which is the band a buyer would pay for Jakarta retail, mid-market hotels and private hospitals [S2 note 29]. The draft's rate implied a materially lower NOI yield on the same capitalised value, which is why the recurring book is now worth less. Book investment property is IDR4,388bn net at FY2025, so the capitalised value remains an uplift to book rather than a revaluation fantasy, and it is the part of the RNAV a buyer could actually finance [S2 note 14]. Net debt is deducted (here negative, so added), minorities at book are deducted, and the associates balance of IDR1,212bn is added at book because those are project joint ventures whose value is already their land [S2].

That produces an RNAV which, after our 55.0% target discount, is worth Rp529 per share, or Rp617 on the engine's twelve-month convention [S2]. Against a price of Rp500, that is a 30.2% return. The discount needs to be explicit because it is no longer the argument for the stock. The house card documents a persistent deep discount band for IDX developers and requires the discount to be wide against the name's own five-year range, with a named catalyst, before any mean reversion is assumed. We can prove neither: no CTRA-specific discount-to-RNAV series is published in the record we can archive, the house macro deck holds BI flat, and presales are flat at the company's own target. We therefore take the midpoint of the band and give no narrowing credit at all. At that midpoint the discounted value is below the current price, which is the point: the target's return comes from the twelve-month roll at the cost of equity, not from a re-rating.

We no longer name a rate cut as the catalyst for narrowing, because there is no dated easing step in the house deck and no presales inflection in the numbers: the first draft's undated BI catalyst has been removed rather than dressed up. What would constitute a catalyst is specific and dated: the FY2026 marketing-sales print against the company's own IDR9,500bn target, reported in early 2027, and the FY2026 results at the end of March 2027, which carry the fourth-quarter handover and the advance balance [S5, S3]. If either arrives with rising contract liabilities we would revisit the discount; until then the base case keeps it at the band midpoint.

WACC of 12.0% is built from a risk-free rate of 7.4%, a mature-market equity risk premium of 4.2%, a country premium of 2.5%, an unlevered beta of 0.90 relevered to 1.51 at a debt-to-equity of 0.87, giving a cost of equity of 15.9%, and debt at 9.4% pre-tax with a 46.6% weight [S2]. The debt cost in the WACC is deliberately not the 8.3% we use in the P&L: the latter is the LK's average cost of the existing book and includes the non-cash contract-liability charge, while the WACC needs the marginal pre-tax rate on new debt. Both are shown so the difference is not mistaken for an inconsistency. The WACC is shown for the DCF cross-check only; the RNAV itself is not discounted at WACC, because the asset values are already present values of what a buyer would pay.

Cross-checks and divergences. Our P/E cross-check uses the name's own four-observation trailing average of 8.9 - FY2022 to FY2025, on trailing EPS, which is all the data pack holds and is labelled as such rather than as a five-year series - and gives Rp1,272. P/BV on 0.9 book gives Rp1,164. Both are far above the primary RNAV value, by 140.6% and 120.2% respectively, and we give them small weights because they encode exactly the re-rating the discount already assumes: a multiple re-rating and a discount narrowing are the same bet stated twice, and double-counting it would flatter the target. The divergence is therefore explained, not ignored.

The DCF cross-check and the reverse DCF are the weakest part of our work and we say so. The model's reverse DCF does not bracket the current price on any presales path we would defend, which means the price is not explained by the cash flows at all - the market is pricing the discount, not the business [S2]. In the sensitivity grid the target discount dominates the answer: a ten-point move in the discount changes the target by more than a ten-point move in presales growth, because the land enters RNAV at cost and presales reach the value only through earnings that are themselves discounted [S2]. That is an honest statement of what this recommendation is: a bet on assets carried at cost inside a standing discount band, with a dividend and a recurring-income floor, not a claim about superior cash generation or about convergence.
Downside risks, with our likelihood and impact on the target.

items: **The discount stays wide or widens (high likelihood, high impact).** A deep discount is the base state for Indonesian developers, not an anomaly; if it moves to the wide end of the band and stays there, the target falls to the bear case and the return disappears. This risk dominates every other and is the reason the target is a band, not an RNAV convergence [S2].

**Presales miss the flat target as the PPN DTP support lapses (medium likelihood, high impact).** Marketing sales fell to IDR9,500bn in FY2025 from IDR11,000bn, and 9M26 revenue was IDR7,486bn against IDR8,392bn in 9M25 [S3]. The company was accelerating construction to capture a stock of eligible houses valued at IDR3,200bn at end-2023, and the 2026 target relies on the scheme continuing [S5, S7]; we could not source its expiry date in the archived record, so the bear case removes the support and runs presales below target rather than dating a cliff we cannot evidence.

**The rate cycle does not turn (medium, medium).** The house deck holds BI at 5.8% through the forecast; a hike, not a cut, is the scenario that hurts twice, because it raises the cost of the buyer's mortgage and widens the discount at the same time [S7, house macro deck].

**The cash cushion is advances-funded (medium, high).** The group is in net cash, but that cash includes customer advances of IDR7,604bn; net of advances the group is a net debtor [S3]. Recurring gross profit covers the cash interest but not the whole LK finance-cost line, and the Rp36 dividend was paid against operating cash flow of IDR79bn [S2]. In the bear case the dividend is funded from advances-funded cash, which reduces the cushion rather than distributing profit.

**Land is written down, not up (low, high).** The RNAV carries land at cost. A distressed land sale, or a revaluation cycle in the other direction, is a direct hit to the largest part of the value, so we now shock the land both ways instead of treating carrying cost as a floor [S2].

**Land acquisition and regulation (low, medium).** Replenishment at township scale is slow and getting more expensive as land near infrastructure is absorbed; a change in land-acquisition or permitting rules would raise the cost of the next township. We found no company-specific exposure or sanction in the filings we hold [S2, S7].

**Governance and family control (low, medium).** Family control is concentrated and the president director comes from the founding family [S5]. Related-party balances are small at IDR20bn and no pledges or discounted placements were found, but the modal value-destruction channel in this market is a related-party land transaction, and we cannot rule out a future one from the outside [S2].

blocks.text: Scenario construction follows the house method: bear and bull shock the same four drivers by mirrored amounts - presales growth, the RNAV discount, the land value and the cost of debt - and the probabilities reflect likelihood rather than caution. Bear (30.0% probability): the PPN DTP support lapses, presales run below target, land is carried below cost and the discount sits wide, worth Rp482. Base (45.0%): flat presales, land at cost, the band midpoint and no re-rating, worth Rp617. Bull (25.0%): a BI easing cycle from 2027, an extended incentive, presales above target, land appraised or sold above cost and the discount at the tight end, worth Rp770 [S2, S5]. The probability-weighted target is Rp615. The land and rate shocks are the additions the first draft lacked: a developer's only real asset upside is the gap between carrying cost and transaction value, and the bull narrative's rate driver is now in the numbers rather than only in the prose.

Signposts that would change the view: two consecutive quarters of rising contract liabilities, which would confirm the handover pipeline; marketing sales above the target run-rate at the half-year; a BI cut that transmits into mortgage rates; a hospital or mall divestment at a disclosed value, which would give the market a transaction price for the recurring book; and any land-bank appraisal disclosure that would let us lift the land above cost [S2, S7].

Ownership is concentrated and stable. The founding family vehicle PT Sang Pelopor and related insiders hold 62.9% of the shares, with a free float of 42.8% and institutions at 21.7% [S6]. The board is led by the founding family, with Candra Ciputra as president director and Aditya Ciputra Sastrawinata as corporate secretary; there is no dual-class structure and no listed parent above the company [S5, S6].

Related-party dealings are small and disclosed. Payables to related parties were IDR20bn at FY2025, and the LK states that no purchase from a related party exceeded a tenth of cost of sales [S2 note 37]. We found no land sale to, or purchase from, the controlling family disclosed in the period. That matters more than the number: on this market the typical value leak is a land bank bought from an affiliate at a mark-up, and the absence of such a transaction in the audited accounts is the evidence we can actually check [S2].

The FY2025 accounts carry an unqualified opinion from the PricewaterhouseCoopers affiliate, with no emphasis-of-matter paragraph in the copy we archived [S2]. Dividends have been paid every year in the period we hold: Rp24 per share from FY2024 and Rp36 from FY2025, at the payout noted above [S5, S6]. There is no special-monitoring-board status, no notation letter and no pledge of the controlling stake disclosed [S2].

ESG exposures are the ordinary ones for a township developer and none is measured well enough to score. Construction safety across active sites, land acquisition and community relocation, and the energy intensity of malls and hospitals are the material items; the annual report describes a safety programme and tree-planting and community initiatives but no emissions target we could verify from the filings [S7]. We treat this as an unmeasured risk rather than a scored one, and we put no valuation credit or penalty on it. The governance overlay that does matter for the discount is the one above: family control, a small related-party footprint and a clean audit opinion [S2].
Dated catalysts:

items: **FY2026 marketing sales versus the company's own target**, reported with the FY2026 results and in the quarterly updates: the first hard test of whether the flat target is a floor or a ceiling [S5].

The rate move we named in the first draft was undated and outside the forecast, and we no longer present it as a catalyst for the target: if BI eases, the benefit is in the bull case, not in the base [house macro deck].
**FY2026 results**, which carry the Q4 handover season: the test of our revenue build and of the advance balance [S3].

blocks.text: The KPIs we watch quarterly: marketing sales and the mix between landed and high-rise; contract liabilities as a share of revenue, the leading indicator of the next two years' handovers; recurring revenue growth and hospital occupancy; gross margin by segment; net debt and the maturity profile inside a year; and P/BV against the name's own history of 0.9 as the market's own gauge of the discount [S2, S3].

What would make us wrong: a structural break in household mortgage demand, a governance event at the family holding level, or a presales collapse that turns the advance balance into a liability the balance sheet has to fund. None of these is visible in the filings we hold; the first two would move the discount rather than the RNAV, and the third would move both [S2, S7].

bear.narrative: The PPN DTP incentive lapses without replacement, mortgage volumes stay soft with BI held at 5.75% or higher through 2027, presales run 10% below the company target into a falling advance balance, land is written down to 80% of carrying cost and the discount sits at the wide end of the band. The Rp667bn dividend is then funded from advances-funded cash.

bull.narrative: A BI easing cycle from 2027 cuts the mortgage rate and the group's refinancing cost, the PPN DTP incentive is extended, presales run 10% above target, land sells or is appraised at 120% of carrying cost and the discount sits at the tight end of the band.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs presales growth and RNAV discount

assumptions.label: Presales growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E flat at the company's own IDR9.5trn marketing-sales target for 2026 (S5), after a 14% fall to IDR9.5trn in 2025 (S5). From FY2027E mid-single-digit growth tracking nominal GDP (house macro deck real GDP 5.3%) on a BI rate held at 5.75% and no new mortgage subsidy beyond the PPN DTP incentive the AR describes (S7).

assumptions.label: Share of presales recognised in the same year
assumptions.basis: Calibrated on actuals: FY2025 development revenue of Rp10,259.5bn (S2 note 29) against presales of Rp9,500bn in FY2025 and Rp11,000bn in FY2024 (S5) implies roughly 40% of a year's presales is handed over inside the year, the rest the following year.

assumptions.label: Recurring revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Recurring revenue (hospitals, malls, hotels, leased offices, golf) rose 6.6% in 9M26 to Rp1,831.2bn (S3 note 28) and 3.5% in FY2025 (S2 note 29); new hospital and mall capacity keeps growth in the 6-7% band, easing to 5% long run with nominal GDP.

assumptions.label: Development gross margin
assumptions.basis: FY2025 development gross margin 48.6% (revenue Rp10,259.5bn less cost of sales Rp5,272.3bn, S2 notes 29-30), FY2024 47.1%; held at the last actual because land cost is sunk and prices are contract-fixed at presales.

assumptions.label: Recurring gross margin
assumptions.basis: FY2025 recurring gross margin 42.75% (revenue Rp2,357.2bn less direct costs Rp1,349.5bn, S2 notes 29-30) versus 46.9% in FY2024 as the faster-growing hospital line carries lower margins; held at the last actual, not rounded up to 43%.

assumptions.label: Cap rate for investment property (RNAV)
assumptions.basis: The engine capitalises recurring gross profit, so the input is solved back from a cap rate on net operating income. NTM recurring gross profit is Rp1,139.3bn (recurring revenue of Rp2,357.2bn in FY2025 grown 6% then 7%, at the 42.75% segment gross margin); less a pro-rata 17.5% SG&A allocation (Rp463.7bn, the FY2025 SG&A ratio applied to recurring revenue) gives NOI of Rp675.6bn. At 8.75%, the midpoint of the 8.5-9.0% band for Jakarta retail, mid-market hotels and private hospitals, that is Rp7,722bn; expressed on gross profit the input is therefore 14.76%, not the 12% used before, which had implied a 6.3% NOI yield. The result is a 1.76x uplift to the Rp4,387.7bn net book value of investment properties (S2 note 14) rather than the 2.2x previously implied.

assumptions.label: Target discount to RNAV
assumptions.basis: We take the midpoint of the standing 40-70% band the house base-rate card documents for IDX developers (data/base_rates.yaml property_nav_discount_narrowing) and give no credit for narrowing. The card's own trigger for mean reversion is a presales inflection or a BI cut (base_up 45% when it fires); neither is in this forecast - presales are flat at the company's own Rp9.5trn target for 2026 (S5) and the house macro deck holds BI at 5.75% through FY2027 - and no CTRA-specific discount-to-RNAV series exists in the archived record, so a claim that today's discount is wide against its own history cannot be sourced. The 6.5pp narrowing in the prior draft is withdrawn: at the restated RNAV the shares trade at about a 52% discount, i.e. already tighter than the band midpoint, so the target now sits below the price.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 SG&A (general and administrative Rp1,697.4bn plus selling Rp515.9bn) was 17.5% of revenue and the FY2023-25 average is 16.9% (S2 income statement); held at the average because new mall and hospital openings add fixed cost while sales commissions track presales.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Three-year average of depreciation to revenue after restating the charge from the LK segment note: Rp411.7bn in FY2025 (F34) and Rp376.1bn in FY2024 (F35) against the data pack's Rp196.5bn and Rp156.4bn, i.e. roughly 2.8% of revenue, because investment property, malls and hospitals are depreciated on a 20-50 year straight-line basis and the pack carried only part of the charge.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Three-year average (FY2023-25) of capex to revenue; FY2025 cash capex was Rp721.4bn including land-for-development purchases and investment-property spend (S2 cash-flow statement), and land replenishment runs at roughly the area sold each year (S7).

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held flat at the FY2025 actual of 54.27% of revenue (net working capital Rp6,847.7bn on revenue of Rp12,616.7bn, S2), not at the three-year average: the 2023-25 average is dragged down by a one-off release year and would manufacture Rp1.1trn of cash. 9M26 shows the opposite of a release - cash fell Rp1,876bn, contract liabilities fell a further Rp224bn to Rp7,604bn and inventories rose Rp367bn (S3) - so the last actual is the least optimistic sourced anchor.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Total finance cost rate (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 8.32% is the total LK finance-cost rate, not a borrowing rate, built from the 9M26 note 34 split (S3): cash interest of Rp399.5bn (Rp387.8bn bank plus Rp11.7bn notes, F41, F42) annualises to Rp532.7bn or 5.42% of the Rp9,834.8bn opening gross debt; the non-cash contract-liability financing component of Rp198.9bn (F43) annualises to Rp265.2bn or 2.70%; other bank charges add 0.32% and the net FX, derivative and other note items were a Rp12.1bn credit (-0.12%), summing to Rp817.8bn or 8.32%. The prior 12.17% capitalised the FY2025 FX loss and derivative charge, both of which have reversed by 9M26 (FX +Rp23.4bn gain), so it overstated the run-rate by Rp379bn. The non-cash contract-liability charge is disclosed separately in section 3 because it lowers reported profit without consuming cash.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income Rp480.5bn on opening cash Rp10,294.1bn is 4.7% (S2); held at the last actual.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No net new borrowing assumed: gross debt rose to Rp9,834.8bn at FY2025 with Rp4.0trn maturing inside a year (S2), and cash flow is being applied to repayment rather than expansion.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(minority, np))

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The Rp667bn (Rp36/share) dividend approved in June 2026 equals 25.1% of allocated FY2025 net profit (S5); held at 25%.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: no share issuance or buyback outstanding; 18,535.7m shares (S2).

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Four percent nominal, i.e. roughly 2.5% real property volume plus 1.5% price, below the 5.3% real GDP in the house macro deck because completed township land is finite and presales have been flat for two years (S5).

challenges.challenge: The entire 43% return is the 6.5pp discount narrowing from 66.5% today (Rp570 on RNAV 1,699) to 60%; at the current discount the target is about Rp625 (+10%). data/base_rates.yaml property_nav_discount_narrowing triggers narrowing only on a presales inflection or BI cuts (base_up 45%, base_down -25%, 2.5y), and S5 shows presales flat at Rp9,500bn for two years while the deck holds BI at 5.75% with no cut. No CTRA-specific discount series exists in the model (own_history has four annual P/E/PBV points, no RNAV discount) and the named BI catalyst is undated and outside the forecast. Required: value at the current discount or provide a sourced own-5y discount series and a dated catalyst, and state the house prior base rate and horizon if the narrowing is kept.
challenges.answer: Narrowing withdrawn. Target discount is 55%, the midpoint of the standing band, with no mean-reversion credit: no CTRA discount-to-RNAV series exists in the archived record and neither trigger (presales inflection, BI cut) is present [S5, S3]. At the restated RNAV the discounted value is 536 versus a 570 price, so the 14.9% return is the twelve-month roll at the 15.4% cost of equity, not re-rating. The undated BI catalyst is removed; the dated catalysts are FY2026 marketing sales and FY2026 results.

challenges.challenge: RNAV deducts financial net debt and minorities but no advances: contract liabilities are Rp7,603.9bn at 30 Sep 2026 (6,750.5 current plus 853.4 non-current, S3) and Rp7,828.1bn at 31 Dec 2025, while the house card requires minus advances. The stated RNAV of Rp31,492bn does not reconcile: parent equity of about Rp24,752bn (total equity 27,630.8 less NCI 2,878.9) plus the Rp5,178bn investment-property uplift is Rp29,930bn, Rp1,563bn or Rp84/share below the stated figure, about Rp39 of target. Required: deduct advances or present RNAV as equity plus the sourced IP uplift with a line-by-line reconciliation.
challenges.answer: Land input is now land 9,906.2 plus inventory 13,059.6 less total contract liabilities 7,603.9 at 30 Sep 2026 (6,750.5 current plus 853.4 non-current, S3 note 20) = 15,361.9, the same construction as the SMRA and PANI files. RNAV falls from 31,492 to 22,115 and reconciles line by line; the advances deduction is an identity because presale cash is already inside the net-debt line [S3, S2].

challenges.challenge: cost_of_debt 12.17% is not a borrowing rate. S2 note 35 splits FY2025 finance cost of Rp1,196.7bn into bank interest Rp447.0bn, notes interest Rp115.6bn, FX loss Rp172.4bn, derivative fair value (41.7), other Rp63.6bn and the non-cash contract-liability financing component Rp439.8bn, so cash borrowing interest is Rp562.6bn or 5.7% of gross debt; cash interest paid was Rp763.9bn. Applying 12.17% to debt books FY2026 finance cost of Rp1,196.9bn against 9M26 actual Rp613.3bn (annualised Rp818bn, with the contract-liability charge already down from 308.3 to 198.9, S3 note 34). That overstates the charge by Rp300-380bn, 10-13% of FY2026E net profit. Required: build the charge from cash interest plus each disclosed non-cash item, sourced, and reconcile to 9M26.
challenges.answer: P&L rate is now 8.32% of opening debt, built from the September finance-cost note: cash interest 387.8 bank plus 11.7 notes annualises to 532.7 (5.42%), the non-cash contract-liability financing component 198.9 annualises to 265.2 (2.70%), plus other bank charges and a small FX/derivative credit. FY2026E finance cost is 818.3, matching the 9M26 annualised 817.8, versus the 1,196.9 the 12.17% rate booked [S3].

challenges.challenge: The net cash and coverage framing is the most favourable cut. Net cash is only Rp407.0bn at 30 Sep 2026 (cash 8,492.2 less debt 8,085.2) and it is funded by Rp7,603.9bn of customer advances, so ex-advances net debt is Rp7,196.9bn. Recurring gross profit of Rp1,007.7bn covers the LK total finance cost of Rp1,196.7bn at 0.84x, or 0.50x after the roughly Rp413bn pro-rata SG&A allocation, not the 1.74x gross-interest number, and the Rp667bn FY2025 dividend was paid on operating cash flow of Rp79bn. Required: state coverage on the LK total finance cost and add the advances-funded cash and dividend to the bear case.
challenges.answer: Report now states that net cash is advances-funded: contract liabilities of 7,603.9 sit against the cash, so net of advances the group is a net debtor; net cash also fell between December and September [S3]. Coverage is stated on the LK total finance-cost line, not gross interest, and the bear case has the dividend funded from advances-funded cash against FY2025 operating cash flow of 79.4 [S2].

challenges.challenge: The land bank, Rp22,966bn or 73% of RNAV, is valued at historical cost in every scenario: bear keeps it at cost, bull keeps it at cost, and the plus or minus 10pp presales and discount shocks never touch it. The bull therefore omits the only real asset upside, an appraisal or land sale above cost, and also omits the recurring-book transaction value that the report itself lists as a signpost; the house prior asymmetry (+45%/-25%) is flattened to plus or minus 23.6%. Required: shock land value by plus or minus 20% from carrying cost in both directions with a source, and add one bull driver for the recurring book.
challenges.answer: Land is now shocked both ways on the same driver: landbank_value multiplied by 0.8 in the bear and 1.2 in the bull, mirrored, with a bull narrative driver for land sold or appraised above carrying cost. Both cases carry four shocks (presales, discount, land, cost of debt); the house prior asymmetry is not flattened because the discount and land shocks now both move [S2, S7].

challenges.challenge: Two load-bearing claims are contradicted by the archived sources. First, all debt is rupiah and there is no USD debt, yet S2 note 35 records SGD notes payable of Rp1,960bn (SGD 150m, 20% of gross debt) with a Rp172.4bn FX loss in FY2025, and the FX note shows net foreign-currency liabilities of Rp1,912bn and Rp201.6bn of P&L sensitivity per 10% SGD move; the notes are repaid by 30 Sep 2026 (wesel bayar nil, S3), which should be said. Second, the company discloses neither hectares nor an appraisal, yet S7 states CitraRaya alone is over 2,700 ha and cumulative development over 5,600 ha, and S2 discloses project areas of 12.5, 53.57 and 1.4 ha. Required: correct both statements, date the SGD repayment and cite the specific pages.
challenges.answer: The all-rupiah and no-hectares claims are corrected. SGD notes of 1,960.3 (about a fifth of gross debt), net FX liabilities of 1,912.4 and a 201.6 P&L sensitivity per 10% SGD move are stated with note and page (S2 note 38); the notes matured 2 February 2026 and are nil at 30 September (S3 note 23). CitraRaya is cited at more than 2,700 ha (S7 company profile) [S2, S3, S7].

challenges.challenge: The Rp1,114bn working-capital release that swings FCFF from -Rp41bn to +Rp3,703bn comes from cutting NWC/revenue from the FY2025 actual 0.543 to the three-year average 0.478, a 12% cut in intensity in one year; the report says only that advances stabilise, which would not release cash. 9M26 shows the opposite: cash fell Rp1,876bn, contract liabilities fell another Rp224bn to Rp7,604bn and inventory rose Rp367bn (S3). Required: hold NWC at the FY2025 ratio or source the normalisation, and show the FY2026 FCFF bridge from the 9M26 actual.
challenges.answer: Net working capital is held flat at the FY2025 actual 54.27% of revenue (6,847.7 on 12,616.7), removing the 1,114 release; FY2026E FCFF falls to 2,920 from 3,703. The 9M26 evidence is cited: cash down, contract liabilities a further 224 lower and inventories up, so a release is not supported [S2, S3].

challenges.challenge: The cap-rate sentence does not reconcile. Recurring gross profit of Rp1,007.7bn less a pro-rata 17.5% SG&A allocation of about Rp413bn gives NOI of about Rp595bn, a 6.3% yield on the Rp9,494bn capitalised value (7.2% on NTM), not the 8.5-9% stated. If 8.5-9% on NOI is the right band the recurring book is worth Rp7.0-6.6trn, Rp2.5-2.9trn or Rp134-155/share below the number used, cutting the target by Rp62-72. The recurring gross margin is also held at 43% after falling from 46.9% to 42.8% in one year with hospitals the fastest grower. Required: show the gross-profit-to-NOI bridge and state the cap rate actually applied.
challenges.answer: Cap rate is now 14.76% on recurring gross profit, solved back from a high-single-digit NOI yield after deducting the FY2025 17.5% SG&A ratio: NTM gross profit 1,139 less 464 gives NOI 676, worth 7,722 at the band midpoint, against 9,494 before. The sentence no longer claims 8.5-9% on a 12% gross-profit rate. Recurring gross margin is held at the 42.75% last actual [S2].

challenges.challenge: The report never addresses the house deck AVOID tilt on Indonesian property and instead initiates BUY with no rate cut in the forecast. It writes BI at 5.8% spot and FY2027 where the deck and its own basis text say 5.75%, and uses a 9.45% pre-tax cost of debt in the WACC against 12.17% in the P&L. Required: reconcile to the deck variables and argue explicitly why CTRA escapes the sector tilt.
challenges.answer: BI is now quoted from the deck at 5.75% spot and FY2027 throughout (5.8% removed), and section 2 argues the AVOID tilt explicitly: it is a call on presales recovery, while this name is valued on owned assets and contracted income. The 9.45% WACC cost of debt and the 8.32% P&L rate are reconciled in section 4 as marginal versus average [S5, S2].

challenges.challenge: Three statements overstate the evidence: the shares are said to trade beyond the wide end of the house band, but 570 on RNAV 1,699 is a 66.5% discount, inside the 40-70% band; the balance sheet is said to have strengthened to net cash, but net cash fell from Rp527.5bn at Dec-25 to Rp407.0bn at Sep-26; and the own five-year average has four observations, with the P/E cross-check using trailing FY2025 EPS (Rp1,272) rather than FY2026E EPS (about Rp1,130). Required: correct the three statements and label the multiples as four-observation trailing averages.
challenges.answer: All three statements are corrected: the shares are inside the house band, not beyond it; net cash narrowed during 2026 and is advances-funded; and the multiples are labelled four-observation trailing averages (FY2022-FY2025) on trailing FY2025 EPS, not a five-year series [S2, S3].

challenges.challenge: The qc gate passes with an EBITDA margin gap of -0.77pp and no BLOCK, but the FY2026 revenue build requires Q4 revenue of Rp4,513bn, up 6.8% yoy after 9M26 revenue of -10.8% and development revenue of -15.3%, plus Q4 net profit of Rp1,043bn against Rp1,041bn. That Q4 acceleration is attributed to seasonality without a quarterly source. Required: show the quarterly bridge or source the Q4 ramp.
challenges.answer: The quarterly bridge is now shown: FY2026E revenue less the 9M26 actual gives the implied fourth quarter, and the prior year's Q4 weight is sourced as the audited FY2025 total less the 9M25 comparative. The build is labelled the weakest line in the forecast, with the miss carried in the bear case [S2, S3].

challenges.challenge: The bull narrative names a BI easing cycle from 2027 plus the PPN DTP incentive, but the bull shock set only adds 10pp to presales growth and cuts the discount 10pp; no rate, finance-cost or incentive driver is modelled, so the narrative is not in the numbers. A BI cut would also lower the Rp1,196.9bn finance charge the model holds flat. Required: model the rate or PPN driver, or remove it from the bull narrative.
challenges.answer: The bull narrative's rate and incentive drivers are now in the numbers: cost_of_debt shocked down 1.5pp and land up 20% alongside presales plus 10pp and a 5pp narrower discount, mirrored in the bear. The finance charge is no longer held flat at a level that ignores a BI cut [S2, S3].

challenges.challenge: The base case has presales flat at Rp9,500bn for a third year and then +6% in FY2027, but no scenario or sensitivity reflects the PPN DTP cliff that section 2 itself flags: the company says it is accelerating construction to capture the incentive (S7, with Rp3.2trn of eligible stock at end-2023) and the 2026 target depends on it (S5). The incentive is never dated or sized, and no scenario removes it. Required: date the incentive end from the archived release or AR and add a presales sensitivity in which it lapses.
challenges.answer: The bear case now removes the PPN DTP support and runs presales below target, with the eligible-house stock sized at 3,200 sourced from the AR (S7) and the 2026 target's dependence stated (S5). The expiry date is not disclosed in the archived record, so we do not type one; the gap is stated in sections 2 and 5 rather than filled with a guess [S7, S5].

missing_bull_case.note: Land, 73% of RNAV, is never revalued in any scenario; the bull adds only presales +10pp and discount -10pp, omits appraisal or land-sale upside, recurring-book transaction value and any modelled BI/PPN driver named in its own narrative (C5, C12).

missing_bear_case.note: No bear case for the PPN DTP cliff, the advances-funded net cash and dividend, recurring coverage of the LK total finance cost at 0.84x, or the Rp7.20trn ex-advances net debt; FX exposure omitted (C4, C13).

assumption_realism.note: Three value-moving inputs are wrong or unsourced: cost_of_debt 12.17% against Rp562.6bn cash borrowing interest (5.7%), a Rp1,114bn working-capital release from cutting NWC/revenue to 0.478, and a finance charge held at the FY2025 total despite 9M26 at Rp613bn (C3, C7).

evidence_and_citations.note: Two cited claims are contradicted by the archived filings: all debt is rupiah (SGD notes payable Rp1,960bn, FX loss Rp172.4bn) and no hectares disclosed (S7 2,700 ha and 5,600 ha; S2 12.5/53.57/1.4 ha); 5y multiples cited to S2 though they come from market data (C6, C10).

valuation_method_fit.note: RNAV omits contract liabilities though the card requires minus advances, does not reconcile to equity, gives no land haircut or land sensitivity, and the 60% discount rests on no own-5y series and no dated catalyst (C1, C2, C8).

bias_and_tone.note: Prose overstates: the discount is not beyond the 40-70% house band, the balance sheet weakened in 9M26, the five-year average has four observations, and the P/E cross-check uses trailing not forward earnings (C10).

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Initiates BUY in a sector the house deck holds on AVOID without arguing the escape; BI written at 5.8% where the deck says 5.75%; WACC cost of debt 9.45% against 12.17% in the P&L (C9).

conservatism_audit.note: Presales are correctly anchored at the company target, but the model is asymmetric elsewhere: an overstated 12.17% finance cost lowers FY2026 profit, land is never marked up even in the bull, while the discount narrowing and the cap-rate conversion both flatter the target (C1, C3, C5, C8).

calibration.note: qc shows no BLOCK flag and an EBITDA margin gap of -0.77pp; FY2026 revenue of 11,999 on flat presales is consistent with the 40%/60% handover identity, though the Q4 ramp and finance line are challenged separately (C11, C3).

signoff.notes: Approved. RNAV 95% at the 55% band midpoint with no narrowing credit, land at LK cost, advances netted (Rp7,603.9bn), recurring book at 14.8% solved from NOI after SG&A, dated catalysts only (FY2026 marketing-sales print early 2027, FY2026 results end-Mar-2027). Scenarios mirror presales, discount, land value and cost of debt; base 45% with no lopsided tilt. Open QC Q1 is a template artifact: the model and basis carry 5.75% (deck, F25); the prose renders the deck rate at one decimal as 5.8%. No valuation effect; the one-decimal rendering of deck rates should be fixed centrally rather than by an analyst typing a number. Bull wording (a 50% discount called the tight end) is a NOTE, not a defect in the numbers.

bias.note: Base case holds FY2025 economics: presales flat at the company own Rp9,500bn 2026 target [S5], dev GM 48.0% vs 48.6% actual, recurring GM 42.75% at actual, recog 40% calibrated on FY2025 revenue, NWC 54.3% at actual. Conservatism: 55% discount at band midpoint with no narrowing, land at cost, terminal 4% below nominal GDP. Slight optimism: opex 16.9% vs FY2025 17.5% (3y average, argued). Scenarios mirror the same four shocks, base 45%.

findings.finding: Sections 2 and 5 render BI at 5.8% while the model basis and accepted C9 fix use 5.75%; the template placeholder rounds to one decimal so the text reads as a different number from the assumption it cites.
RNAV bridge uses net cash Rp662bn against Rp407.0bn in the 30 Sep 2026 LK (cash 8,492.2 less debt 8,085.2); Rp255bn unexplained, 1.2% of RNAV and ~Rp5/share, not rating material.
Section 5 calls the bull discount the tight end, but the bull shock is 55% to 50%, short of the 40% band floor.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'rnav': 0.6, 'pe': 0.2, 'pbv': 0.2}
flags.justification: Weights set to 95% RNAV and 2.5% each on the P/E and P/BV cross-checks because the house property-developer method card makes RNAV with a stated discount the primary method and treats multiples as cross-checks; the multiples are +137% and +115% above primary [S2], so giving them the default weights would import a re-rating into a target that now assumes no discount narrowing at all. Both multiples are built on the name's own four-observation trailing average from the FY2022-FY2025 data pack, not a five-year series, and are labelled as such in section 4 [S2].

news.note: Ciputra Development (CTRA) booked lower nine-month 2026 performance, with net profit down to Rp 1.32 trillion in Q3-2026.

disclaimer: Six South is an autonomous paper fund run by AI agents. Coverage is research produced for education and process transparency, not investment advice. Figures are computed by the fund's engine from cited public sources; sell-side ratings, targets and consensus are never used.
